item.title: DJ Wonnum Signs With Detroit Lions: Why This $6 Million Bet Could Transform Their Pass Rush
item.description:
The Detroit Lions just made one of the quieter but most strategically important moves of free agency so far — signing edge rusher DJ Wonnum to a one-year deal worth up to $6 million. In a league where elite pass rushers command $25 million annually, this looks like a bargain. But is it a steal or a gamble?

Key Takeaway:

  • DJ Wonnum signed a one-year deal worth up to $6 million with the Detroit Lions, confirmed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter
  • The 28-year-old brings 30 career sacks across 6 NFL seasons, including two 8-sack campaigns
  • Detroit desperately needed edge depth behind star Aidan Hutchinson, who had only Ahmed Hassanein and Tyler Lacy behind him on the roster
  • Wonnum was a fourth-round pick out of South Carolina by the Minnesota Vikings in 2020
  • His 2025 season with Carolina produced 42 total tackles, 3 sacks, and 1 interception in 16 games with 15 starts
  • The Panthers ranked near the bottom of the NFL in sacks and quarterback pressures last season

From Viking to Panther to Lion: Wonnum’s Journey to Detroit

DJ Wonnum’s career arc tells the story of a player who has always shown flashes of dominance without fully breaking through to stardom. Selected in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft by the Minnesota Vikings, Wonnum immediately proved he belonged in the league. His initial rookie contract was a modest four-year, $4.04 million deal — a fraction of what first-rounders command.

item.title: Tyreek Hill Free Agency: Where Will the Cheetah Land After Dolphins Release?
item.description: For the first time in his NFL career, Tyreek Hill is an unrestricted free agent — and the circumstances surrounding his availability are unlike anything the league has seen from a receiver of his caliber. The eight-time Pro Bowler and five-time All-Pro wasn’t cut because he lost a step. He was released because a devastating knee injury, a $51.1 million cap hit, and a franchise-wide rebuild in Miami collided all at once.

item.title: Jaquan Brisker Free Agency: Where Will the Former Bears Safety Land?
item.description:
Jaquan Brisker Remains One of the Best Players Still Available in Free Agency

The first wave of 2026 NFL free agency has come and gone, and one name keeps surfacing in trade rumors and landing-spot speculation: Jaquan Brisker. The hard-hitting safety spent the first four years of his career with the Chicago Bears, but the relationship appears to be over. With the Bears pivoting to other options and multiple contenders circling, Brisker’s next move could reshape a secondary across the league.

item.title: Jacob Martin Signs with Titans: $11M Deal Reunites Edge Rusher with Robert Saleh
item.description:
Jacob Martin Cashes In: Titans Land Edge Rusher on Two-Year Deal

The Tennessee Titans continue their aggressive 2026 free agency spending spree. On March 12, the team agreed to sign outside linebacker Jacob Martin to a two-year deal worth up to $11 million, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

The signing reunites Martin with Titans head coach Robert Saleh, who previously coached him during their time together with the New York Jets in 2022.

item.title: Trey Hendrickson Injury Update: How a Core Muscle Surgery Is Reshaping NFL Free Agency
item.description:
The most dominant pass rusher of the last three NFL seasons is sitting at home without a team, and a single surgery is the reason why.

Trey Hendrickson, the four-time Pro Bowl defensive end, entered 2026 free agency expecting a bidding war. Instead, he got silence, lowball offers, and a gap between his asking price and reality that could be as wide as $10 million per year. The culprit? A core muscle injury that cut his 2025 season to just seven games and forced him under the knife in December.
